items.stem: If a holder loses the only private key to a self-custodied cryptoasset, they typically:

options.text: Lose access to the asset permanently, with no reset available
options.rationale: Correct: without the key, self-custodied assets are unrecoverable.

options.text: Can call support to reset the key like a password
options.rationale: Self-custody has no central reset mechanism.

options.text: Keep full access via their email account
options.rationale: Access depends on the key, not an email login.

items.explanation: Correct: without the key, self-custodied assets are unrecoverable.

items.stem: Which two statements about stablecoins are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: They aim to maintain a stable value, often pegged to a currency
options.rationale: Correct: stability against a reference is their design goal.

options.text: Their ability to hold the peg depends on their backing and design
options.rationale: Correct: backing quality affects peg reliability.

options.text: They are guaranteed by governments to never lose value
options.rationale: No such universal government guarantee exists.

options.text: They are all identical in risk and structure
options.rationale: Stablecoins differ widely in backing and risk.

items.explanation: Correct: stability against a reference is their design goal.
